issues.description: Ingest is not atomic; per-row commits can leave a partially refreshed database if parsing or insertion fails mid-run.
Re-ingest never deletes stale rows from results, so removed or absent input records remain in reports.
Harness B assumes every JSONL value and metrics field is an object; arrays, strings, or scalar metrics crash ingestion with AttributeError.
Malformed Harness C XML raises ParseError and aborts ingestion instead of recording a warning or failing cleanly.
Non-finite numeric values such as NaN and Infinity are accepted; NaN scores can crash SQLite insertion and stderr can store invalid values.
Required identity fields are not validated, allowing empty run_id, model, or task values and collisions on blank run IDs.
Harness A ignores and does not validate CSV header names, so reordered or incorrect columns are silently misinterpreted.
The results schema does not enforce score bounds or non-empty identifiers, leaving data invariants entirely dependent on parser code.
Report opens missing database paths through connect(), silently creating an empty database and masking wrong paths.
Fixture generation deletes the user-supplied output directory recursively without a safety guard.
Idempotence tests only cover identical re-ingest and miss stale-row deletion when inputs change.
Tests do not cover malformed JSONL/XML, missing required fields, non-finite scores, missing database reporting, or ingest atomicity.
